sections.overview: This northern raptor breeds across Arctic regions of Eurasia and North America, then moves south into open wintering country.
sections.identification: Feathers extend down the legs to the toes; long wings, dark wrist patches and a pale tail with a dark band aid identification.
sections.habitat: It hunts open tundra and cliffs during breeding, and uses fields, marshes and other open landscapes in winter.
sections.diet: Small rodents, especially lemmings and voles, dominate its diet, supplemented by birds and occasional carrion.
sections.behavior: It often hovers into the wind while searching for prey, and its numbers and breeding success track small-mammal availability.
sections.reproduction: Pairs place bulky stick nests on cliffs or rocky ledges, often reusing or repairing a nest in later years.
sections.ecology: As a predator of small mammals, it responds strongly to prey cycles and occupies an important role in Arctic food webs.
sections.conservation: Its global status is Least Concern, but local abundance fluctuates markedly with prey cycles and winter conditions.
